The shares do not depend on the plate's scale, which is contested (trucksContested): the built gaff is this share of the built lower mast. The peak stands a few px over the cap on the plate, as a long gaff's does.
endurance.hull.masts[2].furlStowProvenance: PLATE READ, r308: when the mizzen sail is stowed, it is brailed in to the mast under a gaff that stays aloft, and the boom stays in place. Two plates of her in the ice show it. (1) Hurley's plate from the starboard quarter (Commons a090007, 1500x1124, about 24 px/m at the stern; crops build/staging/r308/a090007-mizzen-3x.png and a090007-mizzen-foot-4x.png): the gaff stands at its working angle with its vangs hanging from the peak, and the sail is a twisted bundle along the after side of the mast from the gaff's jaws down to the poop. (2) Hurley's beset broadside (RMG P00018, crop build/staging/r308/plate-mizzen-4x.png): the gaff stands at 37.7 degrees (r306's read) and the dark column of the lower mast under it is 10 px wide from the jaws to the rail, against 3 px for the topmast above (median over 70 and 65 rows, build/staging/r308/r308_widths.py). At the plate's 12.4 px/m that is 0.8 m, about twice the mast's own diameter. The main, which r306 read as brailed, measures 15 px against 4 px the same way. Neither plate shows cloth along the boom or a gaff lowered onto it. The boom itself is the record's boomFootM read off plate (1), and Hurley's plate of her heeled in the pressure (build/endurance-heeled.png) shows a spar out over the counter. Plate (1) does not show the boom clearly aft of the mast, so where it lay when this plate was taken is not read; the model keeps it on its topping lift. How the sail was set at sea is not read: the set build draws it on its gaff and boom as before.
endurance.hull.helmProvenance: ON THE FLUSH MAIN DECK behind the bulwark, class station 0.94: the Framnaes section (RMG J9266, 1024x322, ~16.9 px/m, bow at the RIGHT) draws the deck line level to the counter, no poop; Hurley a090007 (starboard quarter, ~24 px/m aft) shows the wall solid to the counter and a man's head over the cap. r272's (0y61) closed as no fault, r273.
endurance.hull.fifeRail.provenance: NO PLATE SHOWS THE FOOT OF THE FORE MAST; the fife rail is drawn to CLASS figures (the rail 1.05 m over the deck, 0.10 over the pin rail; 0.55 m before the mast's skin and 0.85 m abaft it; 0.70 m off each side; posts 0.10 m square; a pin every 0.25 m; a U open aft), and the card says so. Plates read in r280, none of which reaches the foot: Hurley's deck plate (build/hurley-deck.jpg, 1200x858, the SLNSW flickr copy 3535443028 — Commons holds no larger) looks along the deck from amidships and the fore mast's foot stands behind the deck cargo, the winch drum and the kennels; the heeled plate (Commons 4793353650, 4776x3713, RMG P00004, from before the bow) and the Lichtbeelden Vereeniging lantern slide nr. 24 (Commons, 4117 px, the same heel from the port bow) show the bulwark's outside with the deck tilted away; RMG P00013 (4800 px, looking forward from the port bow) shows the cathead and the bow's bulwark only; the full-sail, night and broadside plates show the wall, which hides a waist-high rail. WHETHER THE COURSE HANGS IN JEERS AT ALL on a 1912 hull is itself unread: a lower yard of her date would commonly sit on an iron truss with chain slings, and the builder hangs it in jeers because the hull is wood (S.iron false) — a plate of her fore masthead at a readable scale, or the Framnaes rigging plan, would settle both. A plate of her foredeck from aft — Hurley's dogs-on-deck negatives at SLNSW or SPRI — is the first thing to fetch.
endurance.hull.aftPlatform.provenance: LATTICE PLATFORM WITH A HOODED BOX, read off Hurley a090007 (Commons, 1500x1124; ~24 px/m +/- 3 at the stern from the mast gaps; r273/a090007-stern-6x-ruled.png): cap top row 700, floor row 650 = 2.1 m (+/- 0.3) over the cap, 3.45 over the deck; frame 1.5 m wide, one cross-braced panel a face; box 0.8 x 1.0 m; centre col 910, 0.79 from the mizzen to the taffrail = u 0.99 +/- 0.02, an upper bound. Also in the heeled plate and, wrecked, in LCCN 2013646126. WHAT IT IS is inferred: a hooded box high and right aft is the standard compass on its platform, as Discovery, Nimrod and Terra Nova carried theirs; no source names Endurance's: CONTESTED. Centreline assumed. The rig lifts the mizzen boom over the box: level, its foot is 5.2 m over the deck at the mast, 0.5 m over the plate's gooseneck read (4.0-4.3 +/- 0.4); the cock is residual 0y63.
endurance.hull.stationProvenance: Masts, funnel, deckhouses and overhangs READ off the Framnaes longitudinal-section plan (as Polaris, RMG J9266, web copy 1024x322 px, ~16.9 px/m along the hull — stations good to ±0.5 m, no finer), anchored at the stem and counter LWL crossings; mast-gap ratio and funnel station cross-checked against the Hurley broadside (RMG P00018, ~12.6 px/m: fore-main/main-mizzen 1.12, funnel 45% of main→mizzen). Trucks from the same broadside at 12.6 px/m: fore 34.3 m, main 35.2 m, mizzen 29.3 m over the water, main the tallest — the old record drew the fore at 49 m (27.5 m lower through the square-stack rule) and the main at 31.7. Funnel at 0.677: the plan reads 0.670 +/- 0.015 and the boiler casing must seat inside the house whose forward end it rises from. Funnel black: it reads as dark as the black hull in every plate where masts read pale; height 5.7 m over the rail at the broadside’s scale. No forward deckhouse: the plan shows a boat on skids between fore and main, and no photograph shows a house there. Quarter boats (davitBoats): a canvas-covered boat hangs outboard in radial davits on the port quarter in the Hurley night plate and two stand on the starboard side in the full-sail plate; both plates are bow-on and foreshortened, so the station is bounded, not measured — abaft the aft house (plan, 0.781) and clear of the counter, u 0.80 ± 0.04. Length 6.7 m: the expedition's cutters (Dudley Docker, Stancomb Wills) as recorded; the James Caird measured 6.9. Kept: the forecastle break — the web plan at 16.9 px/m cannot carry a clean break station or height (the deck lines there are one to two px apart); needs the RMG original before it is modelled.
endurance.hull.deck.provenance: SOLID BULWARK, read off the Framnaes longitudinal section (as Polaris, RMG J9266, web copy 1024x322 px, ~16.9 px/m): at midships between the fore and main masts the cap rail's upper line lies at row 176-178 of the copy and the main deck's plank line at row 200, 22-24 px apart, so the bulwark stands 1.35 m (+/- 0.15) over the deck; the cap is drawn 5 px (0.3 m) deep, rows 178-183. The plates agree in kind and cannot give the height: Hurley's full-sail plate (build/hurley-fullsail.jpg, 2828x3912 px, from the port bow) shows a solid bulwark the whole length with a pale cap rail and a pale scrolled band under the cap at the bow; the night plate (build/hurley-night.jpg, 2590x3502 px) and the heeled plate (build/endurance-heeled.png) show the same wall with a lifebuoy hung on it; the beset broadside (RMG P00018, ~12.6 px/m) shows the cap line only, the hull behind ice. hull.freeboard is the SKIN's top in this record (the cap rail over the water, the r215 semantics): it was 2.0, the deck line's own height, and is 3.35 from r272, the cap's; the deck stays at 2.0 m over the water (deck.belowSheerM 1.35), so every mast, house, funnel and boat stands where it stood. The plan's own waterline, the long line at rows 236-238 that runs past both ends, lies 37 px (2.2 m) under the deck line and 44 px (2.6 m) over the keel's underside at row 281; the record's draught of 4.2 m does not match that, and the vertical scale of the web copy is unverified, so the draught is CONTESTED here and not changed (r272). The bulwark is the hull's own planking carried up to the cap, its inboard face the planking's back; stanchions, the pin rail and the scuppers are not drawn.
endurance.hull.capstanProvenance: Bar capstan of the European tradition, a type-period CLASS DEFAULT — no hull-specific plate; counts are class defaults (whelps 6: Falconer 1769 pl. II figs 11-12 resolve six, period range 6-8). Form and proportions from Falconer 1769 CAPSTERN (whelps drumhead-to-deck like buttresses, chocks, two iron pawls, bars heaved at the breast) and pl. II fig 11 (engraving, widths ~±10%: height ≈ 0.86 of drumhead dia, neck sweep 0.82 flaring to 1.0 at the deck). Sized to the men at its bars.

queen-mary-2.hull.tierBands.provenance: DERIVED from a broadside photograph (Paul Coueslant, Southampton Water, geograph.org.uk 5649661, CC BY-SA 2.0, 2018): every tier above the boat gallery is a balcony row, a dark void over roughly two-thirds of the tier height divided at cabin pitch of about 2.6 m.
queen-mary-2.hull.houseProvenance: DERIVED from the same photograph: the black tops out at the recorded 17 m sheer; above it the shell plating carries up two further decks in a WHITE sheer strake with a continuous square-window row on each (shellTiers 2, painted shellTopside), so the boat gallery floor lands at 17 + 2·3.2 = 23.4 m over water — the photograph reads it at about 24 m with the deck module as the scale. The black hull below the strake carries only sparse broken window groups and is drawn plain.
queen-mary-2.hull.shellBands.provenance: DERIVED from the same broadside photograph: the white strake windows are about 1.4 m square at roughly 2.5 m pitch, a bold colonnade, not the 0.7 m C-deck lights the Edwardian default draws.
queen-mary-2.hull.housePlateProvenance: MEASURED off the scale profile (Wikimedia Commons, File:En mary titanic.svg, Yzmo, CC BY-SA 3.0) by segmenting her silhouette and reading, at every metre of height above the load waterline, the most-forward and most-aft column still standing at that height. houseAt fore end, houseCrest, tierForeU, tierAftU 7-8, the funnel station and its 24.3 m fore-and-aft length, and the mast at u 0.19 are all that measurement. Three earlier attempts were judged by eye off a 34-degree lens that magnifies the near half of a 345 m ship by a third. r162: tierAftU 2-6 re-measured off the aft-quarter photographs; see tierAftUProvenance. r163: tierAftU 1 and the houseAt aft end re-measured to the counter (the fantail edge, u 1.008); see tierAftUProvenance.
queen-mary-2.hull.topWorksProvenance: MEASURED from the same scale profile as houseAt/houseCrest (Commons, File:En mary titanic.svg, Yzmo, CC BY-SA 3.0): the runs of her silhouette standing above the 46.5 m top-deck line, each with its u-span and its peak height over the water. Heights here are above the crest roof.
queen-mary-2.hull.deck.provenance: RECORDED for the promenade, EXTENDED above: Cunard's own copy and the Cunard historian Chris Frame carry the wrap-around Promenade Deck, deck 7, as laid teak, nearly 600 m to the lap - and deck 7 is this hull's sheer, so the model's weather deck IS the attested surface. The house tier decks above draw the same covering; photographs of her terraced stern show laid decking there, but no builder's figure attests it. The working foredeck's painted steel is a distinction this one-covering model does not draw. Replaces the deckSteel guess.
queen-mary-2.hull.deck.roofsProvenance: TERRACES, NOT THE CREST: two plates at the era's two ends read laid decking on every aft terrace — the fantail and its pool, the cafe step, the main-pool terrace, the two shallow steps above — and white coated plate on the topmost roof where the dome and mast stand and on the large shell roof forward of the cascade. Plates: Commons 20161001 Queen Mary Aerial 2 (CC BY-SA 4.0, 3888 px, ~3.4 px/m at the stern) and the 2004-07-20 Hamburg arrival set (Arnold Schott, CC BY-SA 3.0, 1200 px, ~1.5 px/m) — colour-field reads, the fields metres wide, so both plates support them; scales and crops in Research/QM2-PLATES.md. Replaces the r108 'false', whose own sentence 'pale coated plate in every photograph' these photographs refute. The forward working deck's painted steel is still not drawn by this one-covering model.
queen-mary-2.hull.rakeProvenance: MEASURED off a bow plate — Wikimedia Commons File:Queen Mary 2 bow.jpg (Conollyb, CC BY 2.5, Sydney) — scaled by her name letters on the flare at about 1.5 m. Her stem overhangs the forward perpendicular by about 23.5 m; the model had 13.67 m, which is why she read blunt from ahead however fine the waterline under her. LOA 345 is fixed and already drawn exactly, so the overhang comes out of the perpendiculars: lwl is the length between them (318.2 m) and the transom keeps its 3.3 m counter — the same lwl-is-LBP semantics r131 established on the container ship and the slave ship. Every u-keyed feature is re-derived through the new frame from its own original plate reading, not rescaled from the old u.
queen-mary-2.hull.tierAftUProvenance: TIERS 2-6 MEASURED off the aft-quarter plates (Research/QM2-PLATES.md), replacing the r97 scale-drawing spans the r132 residual convicted: the drawing dealt seven near-equal steps with the deepest near the top, the photographs read five terraces with the deep ones low and mid. Method: each terrace depth counted in 2.6 m tierBands balcony bays on the 2016-10-01 aerial (CC BY-SA 4.0, 3888 px; every gap measured between deck edges at the SAME height so the one-story parallax cancels), chained downward from the kept crest foot t7 0.816: fantail 6 bays, cafe step 3, main-pool terrace 8, awning step 1, inter-row strip half, top step 5 bays AS BUILT - the record year is 2003 and the 2004-07-20 Hamburg pair reads the open top step about a bay deeper than the 2016 frame, whose refit cabin front took that bay (only the top step changed in the 2016 remastering). Integer bay counts, error a half-bay per edge (1.3 m, u 0.004). Chain closure: the predicted fantail edge lands at u 1.008 against the drawn counter extremity u 1.010. Crest block t7-t9 kept from the r97 profile (not this residual). r163: t1 and houseAt[1] moved to the chain-predicted fantail edge u 1.008 - the 2011 Southampton astern plate reads one continuous rounded shell from counter to fantail rail, and the strake face 0.992 was the scale drawing's stern column (the same weak link as tiers 2-6); the loft rides the counter for any pin past u 1.0. r164: the black paint rise is recorded (sternLivery) and drawn. r165: the balcony wings are recorded (tierWings) and drawn. r166: read 3b measured and closed - tier 7's aft rail curves (tierRound, 2.9 m sagitta), tiers 2/3 measure straight, 4-6 unresolved at plate resolution, and the fantail windscreen is recorded (fantailScreen).
queen-mary-2.hull.sternLivery.provenance: MEASURED off the aft-quarter plates (Research/QM2-PLATES.md). At the stern face the hull black rises over the counter to the foot of the oval-row strake: plate 3 (2011 Southampton astern, 3296 px) reads ONE deck of white below the fantail rail, the name painted on black, and plates 1 (2016 aerial) and 2 (2004 Hamburg, as built) read the same at both ends of the era - so the black swallows the lowest 1 of the 2 white shell strakes (strakes), good to a quarter deck. fromU 0.93 is the knee where the line leaves the level 17 m sheer: ~29 m forward of the drawn tip on the 2016 aerial (the fantail's own 15.6 m span scales the quarter at ~18.5 px/m along-axis), a couple of bays forward of the fantail front 0.959, supported to +/- 2 bays (u +/- 0.016). The line is drawn straight in u from the sheer at fromU to the strake boundary at the stern extremity - the plates cannot adjudicate its exact curve - and the risen black is drawn unpierced: the plates show only sparse small lights in it.
queen-mary-2.hull.tierWings.provenance: MEASURED off the 2016-10-01 aerial (Research/QM2-PLATES.md plate 1, read 3a; instrument build/staging/r165/measure-wings.py): the side balcony wings run aft past each terrace floor, so the terrace sits recessed between them. Wing tips in 2.6 m balcony bays aft of each tier's own recorded face, converted at 2.6/318.2 per bay: tier 4/5, the two-story cabin block on the main-pool terrace, 2.7 bays aft of the tier-5 face (port read, the starboard block corroborates), one tip for both stories, u 0.883; tier 7, the wing decks flanking the top terrace, 3 bays (port and starboard reads disagree 2-5, split and capped by the tier-6 roof they stand on), u 0.840; tier 2, the glazed gallery flanking the fantail, 1.5 bays aft of the pavilion face to its stair, u 0.971. Every read +/-1 bay (u 0.008), tier 7 +/-2. depthM is the wing's inboard extent from the deck edge: the block reads ~6 m (one outboard cabin and balcony, +/-2 m), the fantail gallery ~2.8 m, the tier-7 wing decks ~3 m. The longer lattice-railed runs aft of the block are deck-level balustrades, not enclosed wings, and are not recorded. Wing tips are drawn with a one-bay chamfer at the inboard corner, the angled ends both plates show; the plates cannot adjudicate the exact cut, and the chamfer length is a drawing choice at plate resolution.
queen-mary-2.hull.tierRound.provenance: MEASURED off the 2016-10-01 aerial (Research/QM2-PLATES.md plate 1, read 3b; instrument build/staging/r166/measure-round.py, overlay z-t7-marked.png): the jacuzzi step's aft rail at tier 7 sweeps convex-aft between the r165 wing decks - apex 25 px aft of the chord through the notch corners at ~8.4 px/m along-axis, 2.9 m, +/-1.0 m (apex candidates spread 2.8-3.0 m; the image apex lands 60% along the chord, which is where an arc symmetric about the centreline lands seen obliquely). The SAME instrument reads tier 2 at -0.1 m and tier 3 at -0.1 m: those faces are STRAIGHT within the plate's support, and the r161 impression of curvature at tier 2 was the arch's fan ROOF, not the plan. Tiers 4-6 bunch within 4 m along-axis and tier 6's rail hides under its awnings - unresolved on this plate, not recorded. The fantail edge itself sweeps with the counter since r163.
queen-mary-2.hull.fantailScreen.provenance: READ off both era ends (Research/QM2-PLATES.md): the fantail rail is not an open rail but a continuous translucent WINDSCREEN band under a dark top rail, ringing the swept deck edge. Plate 3 (2011 Southampton astern, 3296 px) resolves panel posts, five horizontal framing lines and a person leaning with elbows on the top rail - the height witness: 1.2 m over the deck, +/-0.2 (regulation floor 1.0 m). Plate 1 (2016 aerial) carries the same band around the sweep at both quarters. The panels lean OUTBOARD (r161 read, both plates); neither plate resolves the angle - 12 deg +/-8 is the drawn lean, an attested direction with a stated bound, not a measured quantity.
queen-mary-2.hull.machineryProvenance: Wikipedia, *RMS Queen Mary 2* (read 2026-11-24, r301), Power plant: four Wärtsilä 16V46CR diesels, 67,200 kW combined at 514 rpm; two GE LM2500+ gas turbines, a further 50,000 kW; generators driving four 21,500 kW Alstom motors inside the podded propulsors, outside the hull.
